ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The golden-haired lion appears both as Mañjuśrī’s mount and as an independently deployed animal in answers, appraisals, contrasts, and verse.
EvidenceBody: The records retain Mañjuśrī riding the golden-haired lion, but also use the animal alone as an answer in public interview, describe its cub roaring immediately on leaving the den, and contrast it with lesser animals: one passage says a supposed golden-haired lion turned out to be a jackal’s kin; another has the golden-haired lion turn into a dog. The lion can also name what a staff-blow becomes: ‘sometimes one blow makes a golden-haired lion.’ These are the corpus’s observable deployments; the entry does not supply a hidden quality shared by them.
